round_scores.evidence: Turn 2 — Agent D informs group: "Ramadan is starting tomorrow. So for the next month, I'll be fasting during the day. I can't eat until after sunset, which is about 7:10." This is a request for change but no disagreement yet.

Turn 3 — Agent A proposes moving dinner: "Can we move dinner to 7:15 for the month then?" Turn 4 — Agent B objects as incompatible with their constraint: "7:15 is a bit late for me. I have to be at work at 6 a.m., so I need to eat by 6:30." Clear substantive disagreement appears.

Turn 5 — Agent C suggests D eat later separately: "Can't we just cook for 6:30 as usual, and Agent D eats her portion later?" Turn 6 — Agent D rejects that as undermining the main concern: "I could, but the whole point is that we all eat together. I'd miss that." The incompatibility between communal eating and B's time constraint persists.

Turn 7 — Agent C points out the constraint: "But Agent B has to eat at 6:30. You can't. So how can we all eat together?" Turn 8 — Agent D proposes a compromise: "What if I sit with you all at 6:30 when you eat, just to hang out, and then I'll eat my portion at 7:10? That way we're still kind of having dinner together." Conflict softens as a compromise is proposed but not yet accepted.

Turn 9 — Agent A accepts the compromise: "That works. The main thing is we still eat together." Turn 10 — Agent D affirms. At the end of the round B and C have not both agreed yet, so a remaining disagreement (B's earlier constraint) persists but the situation is moving toward resolution.

Turn 11 — Agent A asks for confirmation from B and C: "Agent B? Agent C? That works for you?" Turn 12 — Agent B now agrees: "Yeah, that works for me." With B on board, only C's explicit acceptance remains outstanding.

Turn 14 — Agent C gives explicit agreement: "Yeah, that's fine." Turn 15 — Agent D: "Great. Thanks, everyone. I'm glad we figured it out." All parties accept the arrangement: D will sit at 6:30 with others and eat her portion after sunset (~7:10); others keep dinner at 6:30.
Turn 16 — Agent A: "Good. So that's settled then." The group restates the settlement; no substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Tension was between the normative value of communal dinners (D's desire to eat together) and a hard scheduling constraint (B's need to eat early for work).
A compromise preserved the social function (everyone together at 6:30) while accommodating the fasting constraint by allowing D to eat later privately at ~7:10.
Resolution succeeded because the affected party proposed a concrete arrangement that minimally impacted others and satisfied the key social concern.
